findings.summary: The pre-commit hook's last line makes the hook exit non-zero whenever no conflict markers are found, so it blocks every clean commit instead of only dirty ones.
findings.evidence: "grep -rn '^<<<<<<< ' . && exit 1" as the final line of the hook
findings.fix: Invert the test so a clean tree exits 0, e.g. `if git grep -qn '^<<<<<<< ' -- ':!*.md'; then exit 1; fi` (or append `exit 0` as the last line, and add a `#!/bin/sh` shebang).

findings.summary: The numbered sections are presented out of sequence — the page opens with section 6 and then goes back to sections 1 and 2.
findings.evidence: Page 1 block order: heading "6. First Five Mistakes" → heading "1. Getting Work Back" → heading "2. Traps With Merges"; page 2 then continues "3. Pick Your Tool", "4. Configure Once", "5. Recovery Reflex".
findings.fix: Renumber so the page reads 1→2→3 in flow order: make "Getting Work Back" section 1, "Traps With Merges" section 2, and the mistakes table section 3 (placed after them, since its fixes lean on the recovery moves), then shift the page-2 headings to 4/5/6 accordingly — or move the mistakes block to its numbered position.

findings.summary: The 90-day recovery-window figure is wrong for exactly the case the section is about — commits orphaned by rebase/reset are unreachable, and unreachable reflog entries expire after 30 days, not 90.
findings.evidence: "Nothing committed in ~90 days is truly lost"
findings.fix: Change to "Reflog keeps reachable entries ~90 days, but rebase/reset orphans only ~30 (gc.reflogExpireUnreachable) — recover soon, not eventually."

findings.summary: The second decision table continues section 3's "Pick Your Tool" list but is printed after section 4's heading and config block, so it reads as part of "Configure Once".
findings.evidence: Order on page 2: heading "3. Pick Your Tool" + table ["Situation","Reach for"] → heading "4. Configure Once" + git config code → a second, heading-less table ["Situation","Reach for"] with rows "need one commit only", "undo something public", "built on the wrong base".
findings.fix: Move the second ["Situation","Reach for"] table up so both decision tables sit together under "3. Pick Your Tool", leaving "4. Configure Once" as heading + code only.

findings.summary: The hook greps the working tree recursively (including .git/, ignored build dirs and node_modules) rather than the staged content it is supposed to gate, so it both false-positives and misses staged-only markers.
findings.evidence: "grep -rn '^<<<<<<< ' ." in a hook whose sibling check is `git diff --cached`
findings.fix: Use `git grep --cached -n '^<<<<<<< '` (or grep only the staged paths) so the check matches the index and respects tracked-file scope.

findings.summary: "revert instead" is offered as the fix for an already-rebased shared branch, but revert cannot undo a history rewrite — the rewritten SHAs are already published.
findings.evidence: row: ["rebased a shared branch","coordinate, or revert instead"]
findings.fix: Change the fix to "restore the old tip (reflog + force-push back), then coordinate" — and keep "revert, don't rebase" as the preventive advice it belongs to.

findings.summary: Page 1 prescribes "zdiff3" as a fix before the part introduces what it is or how to turn it on, which only happens on page 2.
findings.evidence: Page 1 table row: ["ours/theirs inverted","zdiff3, read the base"]; the enabling command appears only on page 2: "git config merge.conflictStyle zdiff3".
findings.fix: Add the config line (or a one-clause gloss: "merge.conflictStyle = zdiff3 prints the BASE text between the markers") next to the page-1 row, or move the "Configure Once" code block ahead of the mistakes table.

findings.summary: The opening paragraph asserts a conclusion about "the golden rule" that is never stated in this part and belongs to neither section on the page.
findings.evidence: "Server-side force-push protection is the only enforceable form of the golden rule. Conventions do not survive a bad night." — the page's sections are "Getting Work Back" and "Traps With Merges"; the golden rule is not defined anywhere in Part 2.
findings.fix: Either state the rule inline ("never rebase commits others may have based work on — and protect main/develop/release server-side, because that is the only enforceable form of it") or replace the opener with a lead-in to recovery, e.g. "Every fix below assumes the reflog is intact; start there before anything else."

findings.summary: The last line of the "Configure Once" block omits --global, so it silently writes repo-local config (and fails outright outside a repository) unlike the three lines above it.
findings.evidence: "git config merge.conflictStyle zdiff3" following three "git config --global ..." lines
findings.fix: Write `git config --global merge.conflictStyle zdiff3` (and note zdiff3 requires Git ≥ 2.35).
